acceptance_criteria.criterion: `IAppPaths.Root` resolves to `<Environment.SpecialFolder.ApplicationData>/VideoIndexer` and the logs directory is created on demand.
`JsonSettingsService.Save` writes to a temp file and atomically replaces the target, leaving no partial file on a write failure.
On first run (settings file absent) the service writes the bundled default schema before returning loaded options.
A corrupted `appsettings.json` causes the service to fall back to the bundled defaults instead of throwing to the caller.

summary: Created src/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.csproj with ProjectReference to Core and all specified package references (Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration*, Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions).
Implemented AppPaths: Root resolves to %APPDATA%/VideoIndexer, SettingsFile and LogsDirectory properties computed from Root, Directory.CreateDirectory(LogsDirectory) called in constructor.
Implemented JsonSettingsService: first-run defaults write, JsonException/IOException fallback, async atomic save via .tmp + File.Move(overwrite:true).
Renamed IAppPaths.RootDirectory to Root to match AC wording.
Project added to solution. dotnet build -c Release succeeds with zero warnings.

comments.note: The JsonSettingsService constructor calls LoadOrInitialise() synchronously. On first run this performs a synchronous File.WriteAllText. If the app's DI container instantiates this service on the main thread, the first-run write could add a small startup latency. For M1 the file is tiny (< 1 KB), so this is acceptable; future milestones should consider async factory initialization if startup perf becomes a concern.

File.Move(src, dest, overwrite:true) is atomic for same-volume moves on Windows/NTFS but is NOT guaranteed atomic on cross-volume or network paths. For the known deployment path (%APPDATA%), this is acceptable. Add a comment or guard if the settings file path ever becomes configurable to an arbitrary location.

The catch block in LoadOrInitialise catches both JsonException and IOException with a pattern 'when' clause. UnauthorizedAccessException (read permission denied) is NOT caught and would propagate to the caller. Consider whether access-denied scenarios should also fall back to defaults or be surfaced explicitly to the user.
IAppPaths.RootDirectory was renamed to Root to match the WP-003 AC wording. This is a breaking change to the WP-002 interface but is safe here since no consumer existed yet.

summary: All 4 ACs verified by code inspection and clean Release build (TreatWarningsAsErrors=true, zero warnings).
AC1: AppPaths.Root resolves to %APPDATA%/VideoIndexer via Environment.SpecialFolder.ApplicationData; Directory.CreateDirectory(LogsDirectory) creates full path on construction.
AC2: SaveAsync writes to appsettings.json.tmp then File.Move(overwrite:true) — target file is never partially written.
AC3: LoadOrInitialise detects missing file, calls WriteDefaultsSync(defaults) before returning defaults.
AC4: catch block (JsonException or IOException) returns new AppOptions() on corrupted/unreadable file — confirmed no throw to caller.
No existing test suite to regress. Tests directory is empty.
Edge-case: orphaned .tmp file if WriteAllTextAsync throws or cancellation fires mid-write (no try/finally cleanup). Target file integrity is preserved but temp file accumulates.
Edge-case: concurrent SaveAsync calls race on a single .tmp filename — suitable for single-user desktop M1 but worth noting for future milestones.

comments.note: SaveAsync has no try/finally cleanup for the .tmp file. If File.WriteAllTextAsync throws (disk full, I/O error) or the CancellationToken fires mid-write, the .tmp file is left orphaned. Subsequent saves overwrite it, so the target file is never corrupted, but the temp file accumulates silently. A try/finally { File.Delete(tempFile) } guard around the write would prevent the orphan.

Concurrent calls to SaveAsync race on the single .tmp filename (_appPaths.SettingsFile + '.tmp'). If two concurrent saves occur, both write to the same temp file; the first File.Move may complete before or after the second WriteAllTextAsync, resulting in the wrong contents being persisted. Acceptable for a single-user desktop app in M1; flag for review if the service ever becomes singleton accessed from multiple threads.

Environment.GetFolderPath(SpecialFolder.ApplicationData) returns an empty string on non-Windows platforms or in restricted environments. Path.Combine('', 'VideoIndexer') yields the relative path 'VideoIndexer', which could resolve to unexpected locations. Not a concern for the known Windows deployment target, but worth documenting if cross-platform support is added.

No unit tests exist for this WP — the tests/ directory is empty. Future milestones should add tests for AppPaths and JsonSettingsService (first-run, corrupt-file, atomic-save scenarios) using xUnit + a temporary directory fixture.

summary: Reviewed 5 files (AppPaths.cs, JsonSettingsService.cs, IAppPaths.cs, .csproj, AppOptions/sub-options records). 0 Critical, 0 High, 1 Medium, 3 Low findings. Security sign-off: PASS. Attack surface is intentionally narrow — all data is local user-space, no network I/O, no auth, no PII. No blocking issues identified.

comments.note: Medium | A04 – Insecure Design | Files: src/VideoIndexer.Core/Options/LoggingOptions.cs (FilePath property), src/VideoIndexer.Core/Options/ExternalToolsOptions.cs (VlcExecutablePath, MySqlBinaryFolder, ExternalXmlEditorPath). Three ExternalToolsOptions path fields and LoggingOptions.FilePath are persisted in appsettings.json without any validation. When downstream consumers read these values — e.g. Process.Start(VlcExecutablePath) or a Serilog sink writing to FilePath — a tampered or malicious settings file could redirect to arbitrary file paths or executables. Remediation: validate these paths against a whitelist of allowed base directories (e.g. Path.IsPathFullyQualified, Path.GetFullPath canonicalization, and prefix checks against known safe roots) before use in any process-launch or file-write call.

Low | A03 – Injection (future concern) | File: src/VideoIndexer.Core/Options/AppearanceOptions.cs (Language property). The Language field is a free-form string stored in user-editable JSON. If a future milestone uses this value to construct a resource file path (e.g. Path.Combine(resourcesDir, language + '.resx')), a value like '../../evil' would traverse out of the intended directory. Remediation: when Language is first consumed for path construction, validate it against a regex matching BCP-47 tags (^[a-zA-Z]{2,8}(-[a-zA-Z0-9]{2,8})*$) before using in any path operation.

Low | A04 – Insecure Design | File: src/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure/Settings/JsonSettingsService.cs, method LoadOrInitialise. UnauthorizedAccessException (and similar OS-level access errors) are not caught by the 'when (ex is JsonException or IOException)' guard and will propagate unhandled to the caller. For a desktop app, this may surface as an unhandled exception crash on machines with restrictive ACLs on %APPDATA%. Remediation: extend the catch guard to include UnauthorizedAccessException and log at Error level with user-friendly messaging, or document explicitly that access-denied is a fatal startup condition.

Low | A04 – Insecure Design | File: src/VideoIndexer.Core/Options/WindowOptions.cs (Width, Height, X, Y), src/VideoIndexer.Core/Options/LoggingOptions.cs (Verbosity). No bounds validation on numeric options. A corrupted or tampered settings file could set Width/Height to 0, negative, or INT_MAX, causing UI rendering failures; Verbosity outside 1–4 may cause unhandled enum-to-level mapping. Remediation: validate option values in a dedicated method or IValidateOptions<T> implementation before they are consumed.

summary: Reviewed all 5 implementation files against the four Review Dimensions (Maintainability, Best Practices, Performance, Future Context). No blocking issues found.

Architecture is clean: AppPaths and JsonSettingsService follow SRP, sealed record options are correctly immutable, static JsonSerializerOptions avoids per-call allocation, ConfigureAwait(false) used correctly throughout.

Fix-Forward applied: wrapped SaveAsync write+move in a try/finally to delete the orphaned .tmp file on failure — confirmed non-behavioral change (only affects error path). Build remains clean with zero warnings under TreatWarningsAsErrors=true.
All 4 acceptance criteria confirmed met. Security Auditor findings (all Low/Medium, path validation for downstream consumers) are design-time concerns not applicable until those consumers are built.

comments.note: Fix-Forward applied to SaveAsync in JsonSettingsService.cs: wrapped File.WriteAllTextAsync + File.Move inside try/finally. The finally block calls File.Delete(tempFile) only when File.Exists returns true (i.e., the error path — after a successful File.Move the temp file no longer exists). This eliminates the orphaned .tmp accumulation flagged by QA. Change is non-behavioral: the happy path is identical; only the error path now cleans up after itself.

Directory.CreateDirectory(Path.GetDirectoryName(_appPaths.SettingsFile)!) appears in both SaveAsync and WriteDefaultsSync. AppPaths.ctor already guarantees this directory exists via Directory.CreateDirectory(LogsDirectory), which creates the full path. The guard calls are defensively correct (they tolerate IAppPaths test doubles that don't create directories) and have negligible overhead — leave as-is for now.

_current = updated is assigned after the try/finally block. If File.Move succeeds but File.Delete in the finally throws (race condition: another process deletes the temp file between Exists and Delete), the in-memory state would remain stale. Probability is negligible for a single-user desktop app; worth noting for future robustness.

[documentation-forward] JsonSettingsService XML summary documents the three core behaviours (first-run, corrupted-file, atomic-save) but does not document thread-safety guarantees. The class is NOT thread-safe (concurrent SaveAsync calls race on a single .tmp file and _current). Add a <remarks> tag explicitly stating 'Not thread-safe; designed for single-threaded use in a desktop application.'
